sources.title: Belarus's Lukashenko proposes flying with Ukraine's Zelenskiy to Moscow for talks
Lukashenko Offers to Escort Zelensky to Putin, Vows Security
Putin says Ukraine hits Russian oil plants despite Trump’s requests, promises retaliation
Putin says retaliation ‘inevitable’ after Ukraine hit Russian oil plants

en.title: Putin pledges retaliation after Ukraine strikes on Russian oil plants, Lukashenko offers mediation talks
en.dek: Russian leader vows retaliation as Ukrainian attacks continue despite Trump requests; Belarus proposes direct talks between Kyiv and Moscow.
facts: Putin stated Ukraine has continued striking Russian oil plants despite requests from US President Donald Trump to stop
Putin described retaliation as inevitable following the attacks
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko offered to fly to Moscow with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for direct talks with Putin
Lukashenko also offered to act as a security guarantor for the Ukrainian leader
The strikes on Russian oil plants occurred despite US requests for cessation
Direct talks between Ukrainian and Russian leadership have been proposed by a third party
body: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated on Tuesday that Ukraine has continued to strike Russian oil plants despite requests from US President Donald Trump to stop, according to Al Jazeera and The Straits Times.
Putin described retaliation as inevitable following the attacks on Russian infrastructure, the same outlets reported.

Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko offered to fly to Moscow with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to hold direct talks with Vladimir Putin, according to The Straits Times and The Kyiv Post.
Lukashenko also offered to act as a security guarantor for the Ukrainian leader during such talks, the same sources stated.
The proposals for direct talks come as Putin has vowed retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities.
The situation reflects an ongoing escalation in which Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure have prompted Russian threats of retaliation.
en.context: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have been engaged in an escalating conflict involving strikes on energy infrastructure. US President Donald Trump has previously requested that Ukraine cease such attacks. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko has positioned himself as a potential mediator between the two leaders.
